Subject: Question on commit tiers, rollover, and make-goods

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of procurement questions surfaced as we prepare paperwork for legal:

- How does Redwood handle unused commit credits at the end of a quarter vs end of a year? Is there any built-in rollover or do unused credits expire?
- If we under-utilize our quarterly committed tokens, do you provide a make-good (credit/invoice adjustment) or is reconciliation only annual?
- Any standard thresholds you use to determine make-good eligibility (e.g., usage < 80% of committed = credit)?

It would be helpful to see a short example statement showing quarter-by-quarter usage and how a make-good would be calculated. We are aiming to avoid surprises in revenue recognition and budgeting.

Can you loop in billing if needed?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Chen
Head of Procurement, Novus AI

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear questions. High level here and attached is a short draft summary we can include in the SOW (Novus_commit_summary_DRAFT.xlsx). Ben and Jordan are cc'd for sales and billing detail.

Key points (proposed):
- Commit cadence: options for quarterly or annual commitment. Billing runs monthly on actual usage against the committed tier.
- Rollover: we can offer a limited carry-forward for unused credits up to two subsequent quarters (i.e., Q1 unused can be applied in Q2 and Q3 only). Any leftover after that expires.
- Make-good: if total usage over the reconciliation window (quarterly or annual based on elected cadence) is below 90% of committed spend, Redwood can issue a credit equal to the shortfall (committed - used) at the committed rate. For annual commitments we do a single annual true-up; for quarterly we propose a micro-true-up each quarter with a cap to avoid frequent adjustments.
- Thresholds & options: we're proposing a 90% floor by default; we can offer a 85% floor for enterprise deals with a 6% additional discount in exchange for a longer commit.

Ben — can you confirm sales is comfortable with the two-quarter rollover cap and the 90% default language? Jordan — can you validate billing mechanics and whether we need specific GL/AR handling notes for the SOW?

Thanks,
Laura

Laura / Sarah — quick sales note from my side:

- Two-quarter rollover cap is fine and aligns with other enterprise deals; clear cap avoids open-ended liability.
- For make-goods, we prefer issuing a credit on the next invoice rather than retroactive refunds; credits simplify operations and preserve contract values.
- Threshold: 90% default is reasonable. For strategic customers we can move to 85% but request a minimum 12-month commitment and a small premium (1–3% blended).
- Example mechanics (for SOW): Quarterly commit Q = 100M tokens. Actual usage by quarter: Q1=70M, Q2=110M. For Q1 shortfall (30M) — with 2-quarter rollover: Q1 unused can be applied to Q2 usage, reducing Q2 recorded usage shortfall to 0. If after allowed carry-forward total used in the reconciliation window is still < 90% of committed, we apply credit at committed rate.

If billing can provide a sample calculation spreadsheet with the formula columns, we can include that in the SOW for transparency.

Ben

Ben/Laura — billing side details and one ask for legal: see attached usage_calc_example.xlsx. I built a sample that mirrors Ben's Q1/Q2 example plus a quarterly true-up tab. Notes:

- Billing mechanics: we invoice monthly on actual usage. Credits from make-goods are applied as a credit memo on the next invoice after reconciliation completes. We do not retroactively change recognized revenue for prior closed periods; revenue recognition will follow ASC guidance — legal may want to review carry-forward language to confirm.
- Carry-forward accounting: carry-forward is tracked as a notional entitlement; we apply it to usage before computing shortfalls. Any carry-forward that expires is recorded as forfeited credit (not billed).
- Data needed from the customer for statements: monthly usage CSV (token counts per model), PO/contract reference, preferred invoice recipient.

Jordan

Subject: Finalized position for Novus SOW: carry-forward & make-good approach

Sarah — following our internal review, here's a concise summary of what we'll propose in the SOW for Novus AI. If this aligns, we'll update the SOW and route to DocuSign (link below).

What we'll include:
- Commit cadence: Quarterly commitment by default (annual option available), invoiced monthly on actual usage.
- Carry-forward: Unused quarterly credits can be carried forward for up to two subsequent quarters only. Any remaining unused credits after that period will expire.
- Make-good / shortfall: At each reconciliation window (quarterly for quarterly cadence; annual for annual cadence) if realized usage < 90% of committed tokens, Redwood will issue a credit equal to the difference at the committed per-token rate. Credits are applied as a credit memo on the next invoice. For customers electing the enterprise concession (85% floor), we will require a 12-month commitment and a 1–3% blended premium to the committed rate.
- Operational items: Novus to provide monthly usage CSVs (token counts by model) and PO reference. Redwood to produce a reconciliation statement within 10 business days after quarter close.

Next steps:
1) Confirm acceptance of the 2-quarter carry-forward cap and 90% default by EOD Wednesday.
2) I will update SOW and route via DocuSign: https://docusign.com/s/abc123
3) Jordan will attach the usage_calc_example.xlsx to the SOW package for clarity.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you prefer to run through the statement.

Best,
